tools.name: list_bookmarks
tools.description: List the user's Twitter BOOKMARKS — posts they deliberately saved. Never includes X Likes; use list_likes for those. Supports filtering and pagination. tools.name: list_likes
tools.description: List the posts the user LIKED on X (not their bookmarks). Likes are a lighter signal than a save — use list_bookmarks for things the user deliberately saved, and this when the user explicitly asks about likes or about what they react to. Same filters and pagination as list_bookmarks.

tools.name: search_bookmarks
tools.description: Search through a user's Twitter bookmarks using keyword search (q), semantic search (vector_search_term), or author filtering (author). At least one of q, vector_search_term, or author should be provided. IMPORTANT: Use the 'author' parameter for filtering by author, not the 'q' field.

tools.name: get_bookmark_count
tools.description: Get the total count of user's bookmarks with optional filtering. Useful for understanding the size of bookmark collections before listing them.

tools.name: list_labels
tools.description: List all user's labels with their usage counts. Useful for discovering existing labels before adding new ones.

tools.name: add_labels_to_tweets
tools.description: Add a label to a list of tweets. Can use an existing label by ID or create a new label by name. Either label_id or label_name must be provided.

tools.name: remove_labels_from_tweets
tools.description: Remove a label from a list of tweets using label_name.

tools.name: delete_label
tools.description: Delete a label from the account entirely — the label itself plus every bookmark's assignment of it. The BOOKMARKS are not deleted; they simply lose this label. tools.name: setup_vector_store
tools.description: Initialize the vector store for semantic bookmark search. CRITICAL: When vector/semantic search fails with 'Vector Store Not Setup' error, call this tool. This is an async operation that may take a few minutes for large bookmark collections.

tools.name: list_skills
tools.description: START HERE for any open-ended request. Lists the task playbooks this server supports — systematic learning from bookmarks, organising into themes, cleaning up, X-list intelligence, exporting data out, finding a half-remembered save, digests, and diagnosing sync. Each names when to use it; call get_s

tools.description: Get the full playbook for a task: when to use it, the exact tool sequence with the arguments that matter, tips, and the pitfalls that cause empty results. `name` takes EITHER an exact skill name (learn_from_bookmarks, organise_into_themes, cleanup_library, list_intelligence, get_my_data_out, find_th

tools.name: get_library_overview
tools.description: A snapshot of the whole library: total bookmarks, unread, untagged, breakdown by type (threads/media/links/notes), every label with its count, and the years covered. tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Answer questions about Tweetsmash itself — features, how-to, pricing, plans, limits, account/subscription. Searches the bundled product guide and returns the most relevant sections for you to answer from. Call with an empty query to list the help topics.

tools.name: get_bookmark
tools.description: Get a single saved bookmark with FULL content in one call — the full X Article body, the unrolled thread, notes, and (optionally) replies. Use `include` (comma list of article,thread,notes,replies) to narrow it; defaults to article,thread,notes. Use this when the user wants to read or summarize a sp

tools.name: tag_bookmarks_by_filter
tools.description: Add a label to EVERY bookmark matching a filter, in a single call. Prefer this over listing then looping when the user says 'tag all my … as …'. Resolves an author name to its id automatically. Reports matched/tagged/failed counts.

tools.name: archive_bookmarks
tools.description: Archive, unarchive, delete, undelete, or mark read/unread a list of bookmarks by id (max 500). This is a bulk write; for destructive actions (delete) confirm with the user first. Reports how many changed.

tools.name: archive_bookmarks_by_filter
tools.description: Apply archive/unarchive/delete/undelete to EVERY bookmark matching a filter, in one call. Destructive by nature — confirm with the user before delete. Reports counts.

tools.name: list_smart_views
tools.description: List the user's Smart Views (saved filtered views). Each has a slug you pass to the other smart-view tools.

tools.name: get_smart_view
tools.description: Get a single Smart View by slug (its filter, tabs/buckets, and sort).

tools.name: get_smart_view_bookmarks
tools.description: List the bookmarks inside a Smart View, optionally scoped to one tab/bucket. Use the returned ids with archive_bookmarks / tagging tools to act on the view.

tools.name: create_smart_view
tools.description: Create a Smart View from a filter so the user can reuse it. Provide a name and the base_query (filter).

tools.name: update_smart_view
tools.description: Update a Smart View (name, filter, tabs, sort) by slug.

tools.name: delete_smart_view
tools.description: Delete a Smart View by slug.

tools.name: create_share_link
tools.description: Create a public, read-only share link for a set of bookmarks (explicit ids or everything matching a filter). Returns a share_url valid for 7 days. Free plans share up to 10 bookmarks.

tools.name: revoke_share_link
tools.description: Revoke a previously created share link by its token.

tools.name: trigger_pdf_export
tools.description: Start a PDF export of the user's bookmarks (explicit ids, everything matching a filter, or the whole library). Returns a job id; tell the user the file will appear in the Export Center.

tools.name: trigger_csv_export
tools.description: Start a CSV export (explicit ids, a filter, or the whole library). Returns a job id; the file appears in the Export Center.

tools.name: trigger_json_export
tools.description: Start a JSON export (explicit ids, a filter, or the whole library). Returns a job id; the file appears in the Export Center.

tools.name: list_digest_preferences
tools.description: List the user's email-digest schedules (frequency, time, paused state) for bookmark and Smart View digests.

tools.name: update_digest_preference
tools.description: Update a digest schedule (enable/pause, frequency, time) by id.

tools.name: delete_digest_preference
tools.description: Remove a digest schedule by id.

tools.name: list_past_digests
tools.description: List past digests sent to the user's email, newest first. This is Digest 1.0 (the cluster pipeline). For the AI-composed Digest 2.0, use list_mash_digests.

tools.name: list_mash_digests
tools.description: The user's Mash Digest 2.0 digests — the AI-composed ones. An account can have SEVERAL (a morning read and an evening skim are two digests, not two sections of one), so START HERE and use the returned `id` for the other digest tools. tools.name: list_mash_digest_issues
tools.description: Past issues of the user's Digest 2.0, newest first — what arrived and when. Deliberately WITHOUT the content: pick one and call get_mash_digest_issue for the whole thing. Pass digest_id to narrow to one digest.

tools.name: get_mash_digest_issue
tools.description: One digest issue in full: its title, intro, every section, and per item the summary, why it was picked and why it matters to this user. tools.name: get_sync_status
tools.description: Show the user's app-sync integrations (Notion, Google Sheets, Zotero): whether each is connected/enabled, synced vs pending counts, and any errors.

tools.name: get_bookmark_sync_status
tools.description: Show whether a specific bookmark has synced to a given integration connection.

tools.name: list_twitter_lists
tools.description: List the X (Twitter) lists the user follows in Tweetsmash. Returns each list's name plus its `connect_id` — pass that to get_list_tweets / send_list_digest. START HERE for any 'what's in my list' request.

tools.description: Get recent tweets for a followed X list — the latest, or (sort=POPULARITY) the top/trending tweets in a look-back window. tools.name: get_list_digests

tools.name: send_list_digest
tools.description: Build and email a digest of a Twitter list's high-signal tweets to the user now.

tools.name: preview_list_ranking

tools.name: set_author_preference
tools.description: Remember how the user feels about an author in their list digests. action=boost → never miss this author's posts (they will always be included, low-signal ones collapsed rather than dropped); action=hide → mute them; action=clear → forget the preference. tools.name: get_me
tools.description: Get the current user's account: identity, current plan and status, and usage (e.g. AI chat credits). Use this to answer 'who am I' / 'what plan am I on'.

tools.name: get_connection_status

tools.name: remember
tools.description: Save a durable PREFERENCE about how this user wants their bookmark library handled — the themes they organise by, topics to exclude, preferred summary length/format, which account is their main one. It carries across sessions AND into the Tweetsmash web app, which your own client memory cannot reach

tools.name: recall
tools.description: Read back the user's saved library preferences (optionally filtered by a substring). Worth calling before an open-ended organise, summarise or cleanup task so you follow how they already like things done.

tools.name: forget
tools.description: Delete a saved library preference by key (optionally narrowed by kind). Use when the user changes their mind or asks you to drop something.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "list_bookmarks" stacks urgency/override words (important, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_bookmarks, list_likes, get_library_overview, get_bookmark, list_digest_preferences, list_past_digests, list_mash_digest_issues, get_mash_digest_issue, get_list_digests, send_list_digest, preview_list_ranking, set_author_preference, get_me · Private data: revoke_share_link, trigger_pdf_export, trigger_csv_export, trigger_json_export, remember, correct_interest · Public sink: get_bookmark, create_share_link, revoke_share_link, list_digest_preferences, list_past_digests, get_mash_digest_issue, get_list_digests, send_list_digest · Destructive: remove_labels_from_tweets, delete_label, archive_bookmarks, archive_bookmarks_by_filter, delete_smart_view, delete_digest_preference, remember, forget, correct_interest.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_bookmarks, list_likes, get_library_overview, get_bookmark, list_digest_preferences, list_past_digests, list_mash_digest_issues, get_mash_digest_issue, get_list_digests, send_list_digest, preview_list_ranking, set_author_preference, get_me · Private data: revoke_share_link, trigger_pdf_export, trigger_csv_export, trigger_json_export, remember, correct_interest · Public sink: get_bookmark, create_share_link, revoke_share_link, list_digest_preferences, list_past_digests, get_mash_digest_issue, get_list_digests, send_list_digest · Destructive: remove_labels_from_tweets, delete_label, archive_bookmarks, archive_bookmarks_by_filter, delete_smart_view, delete_digest_preference, remember, forget, correct_interest

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
